tasks.title: Audit the whole system: code and docs must ask for a reference type, never name a provider
tasks.notes: 2026-10-20: provider_name_audit + check_provider_names.py + baseline; pre-commit guard for *new* violations. docs/provider-name-audit.md (classify a/b/c, burn-down order). Baseline 138 after second scripts wording pass (266→138; was 446 start). Remaining mostly (b): identifiers (osm_way_id, OSMIndex, OSMGround, google var), paths (reference/osm), imports (defra_lidar/defra_world), lidar_heightmap/ground_layer code, bake-off susu scripts, 28 docs/ ADR archive. Type-driven seams next. Types and providers are two distinct layers (GLOSSARY: Type, Provider). Find every place that names a provider where it means a type, and move it behind the type: e.g. 'DEFRA' / 'defra_lidar' / 'UKDEFRA' where the need is a DTM or DSM (lidar height), 'google' / 'streetview' where the need is aerial or street-level photo, 'OSM' where the need is vector_map, 'Geocraft'/'pristine' where the need is a ground or height reference. Scope: scripts and tools (imports, hard-coded paths and cache dirs such as downloads/defra-lidar, function and module names), config (world-frame elevation_plugin, place-sources), rules, skills, AGENTS.md, briefs and docs (wording that tells a model to use a vendor). Method: grep for provider/vendor names outside providers/<id>/ and config/*providers*.json; classify each hit as (a) legitimate provider-internal, (b) should resolve a type to a provider per place via config, (c) wording only. Deliver: the hit list with classification, fixes for (b) and (c), and a check (test or lint script) that fails when a provider name appears outside provider packages and provider catalogues. Why: long-term flexibility, so any place can use its own national or local provider for the same type. Related: the lidar provider layer (scripts/lidar_provider.py in Southampton Refine) is the pattern to generalise; coordinate with that work before starting.
